# `•explain` — Explain

`•explain text` runs `text` in the caller's scope, as `⍎` does, computes its result, and gives a record of that result and of what happened while it ran and computed it. Code that another thread runs meanwhile records into the same report. Computing a pending result at the end makes no `forced` row:

- `value` is the result of `text`.
- `fused` has a row for each fused group that ran, as [`•prefs`](prefs.qmd) describes fusion. `glyphs` lists the glyphs of the group's calls in the order they ran. A fold that reads through the group, without building it, adds its glyph last. `items` is the group's item count. `blocks` counts the blocks of items that the group ran in turn. `runs` counts the pieces of work that those blocks split into. A block splits where it crosses the end of a long repeat or cycle in an input, as in adding a row of 5,000 items to every row of a matrix. More runs than blocks means the group ran in smaller pieces. `copied` counts the items copied out of inputs before the calls read them, as a reversed read needs. A `copied` of 0 means the group read every input in place. `compiled` is `$t` where the group ran compiled code: machine code made for the group's calls and types. Calls that have machine operations giving their kernels' results exactly, such as `+`, `-`, `×`, `⌈` and `⌊` on floats, compile together where two or more come one after another, or where they are all of the group's calls. The other calls run on their usual kernels. A group compiles where a group of the same calls on the same types ran before, or where it has about 3 million items or more. The browser build compiles nothing.
- `compiles` has a row for each piece of a group's code that compiled. `glyphs` lists the group's calls, and `microseconds` is the compile's time, about 250 for a group of a few calls.
- `stored` has a row for each pending array that a fused group read as an input after computing it on its own. `glyphs` gives the glyph of the call that computed it, which a copy, such as a reversal, doesn't have. `items` is its item count. `reason` says why the group didn't compute it as one of its calls:
  - `"held outside the group"`: it's a copy that a name or another array also holds. A group computes any other pending array that a name or another array holds as one of its outputs, storing the array's items in the same pass, and gives it no row. A dfn's local, `⍵` or `⍺` stops holding its array at the dfn's last read of it. It holds the array until the dfn returns where a nested dfn or an error guard's handler mentions the name, or where the dfn reads names by text, as `⍎` does.
  - `"kept by a fold"`: a fold left its calls in it, to compute later.
  - `"a kind that the group doesn't hold"`: its items are of a type that a group doesn't hold, such as complex numbers.
- `forced` has a row for each call or assignment that computed items of pending arrays. Computing an array ends its fusion. `function` is the call's function, or `←` for an assignment that computed one by writing into it, displaying it with `⎕←` or destructuring it. `line` and `column` give its position in `text`, and `items` is how many items it computed. A selection of a few items, such as `↑r` or `2↑r`, reads a pending copy from its source and computes nothing. From a pending result that nothing else holds, such as `2×y+1` in `5↑2×y+1`, it computes only the items it reads. A pending result that a name holds is computed whole on its first read, and keeps its items for later reads.
- `fast` has a row for each [fast combination](../terms.qmd#term-fast-combination) taken, and for each fold of [windows](../glyphs/up-down-arrow.qmd) that slides over their source without building them. `combination` names it, and `function` is the function that took it. The names are `"partial grade"`, `"partial sort"`, `"ranks"`, `"group counts"`, `"group folds"`, `"determinant"`, `"permanent"`, `"masked select"` and `"sliding fold"`.
- `accumulations` has a row for each sum that added items at positions an index gave them, as the gradient of a selection that repeats positions does under [`∂`](../glyphs/partial.qmd), and for each modified assignment to a selection, as `z.[p]+←1` makes. Positions in one ascending run add a block and make no row. `items` is how many items it added, and `size` is its result's item count. The gradients of reversal, rotation, take, drop, transpose, windows that move by 1, and `⌈` and `⌊` folds read the cotangent instead, and make no row. `path` names how the items were added:
  - `"in place"` adds into the array, with nothing to undo.
  - `"logged"` keeps each target's old item, to restore the array if a target fails. Exact integers take this path, because a sum can overflow.
  - `"on a copy"` converts the array first, as for 16-bit floats, or for Booleans that get numbers. Exact integers that get floats stay exact beside them, so they take `"rounds"` or `"one call"`.
  - `"rounds"` makes one call for each repeat of a position.
  - `"one call"` makes one call for targets at distinct positions.
  - `"item by item"` calls the function once for each target, as a dfn does.
- `fallbacks` has a row for each [map](../terms.qmd#term-map) that called its operand once for each cell after its [batched call](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects) fell back, or without a batched call because an earlier one stopped. `items` is the number of cells, and `reason` says why:
  - `"an effect"`: the operand writes output, reads input, formats a cell's value with `⍕`, or runs a system function that acts, such as `•nget` or `•time`. A batched call would do each of these once for all the cells.
  - `"a write"`: the operand writes to a name outside the map, or a side of a guard on a cell's value writes to a name outside its dfn, or the operand appends to a value that differs from cell to cell, or writes into one so that it would be held in mixed storage.
  - `"a cell's value"`: the operand reads a cell's value to give a count or a position, as `2×⍣⍵` does. A predicate on a cell's value doesn't stop the batched call: each side of the guard runs once, on the cells that take it, as [Evaluation](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects) describes.
  - `"no batch rule"`: the operand calls a function with no rule for batches of these arguments, such as `∪`, or the two sides of a guard on a cell's value give results of different kinds or shapes. Where the stop comes from a primitive's call, the primitive's glyph follows, as in `"no batch rule for ∪"`. A kernel that reads a cell's number directly gives no glyph.
  - `"too many items"`: a call would repeat an array that every cell shares into far more items than its arguments hold, and the array is too large for the map to run on chunks of cells instead, as [Evaluation](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects) describes.
  - `"a caught error"`: a guard would catch an error.
  - `"a recursive call"`: a guard on a cell's value runs in a recursive call of a dfn whose guard already split the cells, as in `{⍵<2?⍵;∇⍵-1 + ∇⍵-2}¨v`.
  - `"an earlier stop: "` and one of the reasons above: the operand is a dfn whose batched call stopped on an earlier call, for a cause that would recur, as [Evaluation](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects) describes. The map calls it once for each cell without trying a batched call.
  - `"an error"`: the batched call failed. The calls on each cell then report the error, if one of them fails.
  - `"the result"`: the operand's result wasn't a batch of the cells' results, such as a function. A strand counts as one batch where each of its items holds an atom for each cell and the items' kinds join. So a strand that holds a vector for each cell falls back, and so does one that mixes numbers and characters.
- `mixed` has a row for each write that left a compact array in mixed storage, as writing an exact integer among floats does under dynamic kinds, by [the write rule](../numbers.qmd). `code` is the target or call that wrote, and `line` and `column` give its position in `text`. `target` names the array's storage before the write, and `written` the storage of the values written, as [`•storage`](storage.qmd) names them. `items` is the array's item count.
- `itemwise` has a row for each route that handled an array's items one at a time, where whole-array code runs most calls. `function` is the innermost call that ran it, the target of a selective assignment, or `•explain` for a route outside both, and `line` and `column` give its position in `text`. `items` is how many items the route handled, and `route` names it:
  - `"item pairs"`: a pervasive function called itself on each pair of items of mixed storage or of a nested array.
  - `"batched items"`: code with no rule for batches read a batch's items one at a time, even where the batched call then succeeded.
  - `"∂ items"`: code with no rule for [`∂`](../glyphs/partial.qmd) read the items of a value that `∂` tracks one at a time.
  - `"accumulation"`: a sum added items one at a time, as the `accumulations` path `"item by item"` does.
  - `"item lanes"`: a fold or scan by a function with no kernel for its arguments, such as a primitive on mixed storage or a dfn on a lane that no batched map took, called the function on each pair of items in turn.
  - `"number parts"`: monadic [`∨`](../glyphs/vee.qmd) or [`∧`](../glyphs/wedge.qmd) took the parts of integers or exact numbers one at a time, where floats and complex numbers take one pass.
  - `"nested labels"` and `"label ids"`: a selection from a nested array labelled or placed its items one at a time.
  - `"key groups"`: [Key](../glyphs/quad-equal.qmd) called its operand once for each group, where no fast combination covered it.
  - `"batch cells"`: a batched map ran a system function, or a deal by [`¿`](../glyphs/inverted-question.qmd), once for each cell in turn.
  - `"inverse scan"`: the inverse of a scan by a function with no kernel called the function's inverse on each pair of neighbouring items in turn.
- `declined` has a row for each faster route that code considered and didn't take. A decline explains why a slower route ran. `route` names the route, `reason` says why code didn't take it, and `items` counts the items that its declines concerned, summed for each route and reason. The routes are:
  - `"fusion"`: a call that could have joined a fused group ran on its own, because of `"an exact argument"` or `"an argument of another kind"`. A call whose result's type depends on its items, such as one on ordinary integers under dynamic kinds, never joins a group, and makes no row.
  - `"fused fold"`: a fold computed its argument instead of reading through its group, because the argument is `"a copy that no call moves under"`, or because of `"a fold that its group can't run"`. A fold of a pending array that a name also holds stores the array's items in the same pass.
  - A fast combination's name, as in `"partial grade"`, with `"arguments that don't suit it"`: the general path ran instead.
  - `"batching"`: a map didn't try a batched call, because `"the batch pref is off"`, because of `"a label level, or a ∂ call inside a batched run"`, or because of `"an argument too large to lay over the frame"` or `"an argument that isn't compact"`.
  - `"program"`: [`∂`](../glyphs/partial.qmd) ran without a program, and `reason` says why. `"a call under another level"` means `∂` ran inside another level, such as a batched map. `"an argument that programs can't hold"` means a program can't take one of `∂`'s arguments. `"a free value that changes on every call"` means that the function reads a name from outside its body, or binds an array, as positions, a count or a guard, and that value was new on several calls in a row. `"a function called on each item"` means that the function calls a function once for each item of a traced array, as a fold by a dfn or Each through a guard does. Any other reason is the reason that the trace stopped, on this call or on an earlier call with the same argument types and shapes, such as `"an effect"`. `items` counts the items of `∂`'s right argument.
  - `"in place"`: a kernel copied an argument's items into a buffer instead of reading them where they are, because of `"repeats of each item"`, `"a cycle that wraps"`, `"steps other than a forward run"` or `"a repeated item"`.
- `programs` has a row for each [`∂`](../glyphs/partial.qmd) that ran from a program, which holds the whole call, its value and its derivative together. `event` is `"built"` where the call's trace built the program first, and `"replayed"` where the call found one. `steps` counts the program's steps. `blocks` counts the block stages that the call ran: each run of elementwise steps on values of one item count, with a fold that reads them, runs as one block stage, a block of items at a time. `compiled` counts the stages that held compiled code after the call. A program's first reuse compiles each stage whose calls can compile, as `fused`'s `compiled` describes. Block stages compute 32-bit and 64-bit floats, Booleans, and integers that wrap. A program's sums can differ in their last bits from the steps run one at a time, and from one call to the next. `listing` shows the program, one line for each value. It shows a size mark in the dfn as a `convert` step. A call whose trace stopped has a `declined` row instead.

Each of `fused`, `compiles`, `stored`, `forced`, `fast`, `accumulations`, `fallbacks`, `mixed`, `itemwise`, `declined` and `programs` is a record of columns, as `•csv` gives a table, so `(•explain t).fast.combination` lists the combinations taken. `•prefs ["fusion":$t]` writes each forcing call and assignment as it happens. Nothing is recorded outside `•explain`.

```bpl
y←¿1000000⍴0
(•explain "+/ 2×y+1.5 - 1").fused            ⍝ ["glyphs":["+×-+/"] "items":[1000000]ₓ "blocks":[245]ₓ "runs":[245]ₓ "copied":[0]ₓ "compiled":[$f]]
e←•explain "≢⍕ 2×y+1.5 - 1"
e.forced.function                            ⍝ ["⍕"]
e.fused.glyphs                               ⍝ ["+×-"]
(•explain "2×⌽y+1").fused.copied             ⍝ [1000000]ₓ
t←y-0.25 ⋄ (•explain "t×1-t").fused.glyphs    ⍝ ["--×"]
q←1000005↑1⌽y ⋄ (•explain "+/q+1").stored    ⍝ ["glyphs":[""] "items":[1000000]ₓ "reason":["held outside the group"]]
(•explain "5↑2×y+1").forced.items            ⍝ [5]ₓ
s←2×y+1 ⋄ (•explain "5↑s").forced.items      ⍝ [1000000]ₓ
r←⌽y ⋄ (•explain "r.[0]←0").forced.function   ⍝ ["←"]
(•explain "(10↑)∘⍋ y").fast.combination     ⍝ ["partial grade"]
x←¿1000⍴0 ⋄ p←¿1000⍴1000
(•explain "{+/, 3↕⍵ (×⍤1) 1 2 1}∂ x").accumulations  ⍝ ["items":⍬ₓ "size":⍬ₓ "path":0⍴⊂""]
(•explain "{+/⍵.[p]}∂ x").accumulations            ⍝ ["items":[1000]ₓ "size":[1000]ₓ "path":["in place"]]
z←1000⍴0ₓ ⋄ (•explain "z.[p]+←1ₓ").accumulations.path  ⍝ ["logged"]
(•explain "{2(×⍣⍵)1}¨⍳5ₓ").fallbacks  ⍝ ["reason":["a cell's value"] "items":[5]ₓ]
w←4⍴0.5 ⋄ (•explain "(⍳2ₓ)@[1 3] w").mixed  ⍝ ["code":["(⍳2ₓ)@[1 3]"] "line":[1]ₓ "column":[1]ₓ "target":["float64"] "written":["integer"] "items":[4]ₓ]
m←1ₓ 2.5 ⋄ (•explain "m+1").itemwise  ⍝ ["function":["+"] "line":[1]ₓ "column":[2]ₓ "route":["item pairs"] "items":[2]ₓ]
(•explain "+/⌽y").declined  ⍝ ["route":["fused fold"] "reason":["a copy that no call moves under"] "items":[1000000]ₓ]
```

[`•memory`](memory.qmd) reports the live record nodes and pending arrays, and what a value keeps alive.
